nodes.label: Geospatial Query Strategy (geohash5/geohash6 prefix filtering)
nodes.rationale: Geohash-prefix filtering at two precisions retrieves candidate events via SQLite index scans, with final bounding-box filtering done in the Worker for precise radius — avoids client-side filtering and leverages indexes efficiently.

nodes.label: Pre-publish duplicate check (Levenshtein + LLM probability)
nodes.rationale: Checking nearby existing events (±1h, 0.1km) via title-similarity plus an LLM duplicate-probability call before publishing avoids relying solely on the API's 409 response; if the LLM check errors, it fails open (treated as not-duplicate) so the worker's own dedup logic remains the final authority.

nodes.label: Duplicate Event Detection — Two-Stage Pipeline (Levenshtein + LLM)
nodes.norm_label: duplicate event detection — two-stage pipeline (levenshtein + llm)
nodes.rationale: Fast structural gates (distance, time, Levenshtein fast-path) run before any LLM call to keep the common case cheap; the LLM stage is only invoked when structural signals are ambiguous, and is given geo+time context explicitly so it can weigh title differences correctly (e.g. same festival, different subtitle).

nodes.label: Nine-cell geohash neighborhood duplicate check
nodes.rationale: Two events at the same venue can land in adjacent geohash cells if coordinates sit near a cell edge; querying only the center cell would miss those comparisons, so the duplicate check queries the center cell plus its 8 neighbors.

nodes.label: Two geohash precisions for radius queries
nodes.community_name: Tracing an Event from Browser to Database
nodes.norm_label: two geohash precisions for radius queries
nodes.rationale: D1/SQLite has no spatial index type, so the worker stores geohash5 (~5km) and geohash6 (~1.2km) per event; a radius query hashes the center at the matching precision, assembles the nine-cell neighborhood, fetches candidates, then applies a Haversine filter. geohash6 is used for small radii (<=5km), geohash5 for larger ones.

nodes.label: Event ID = SHA-256 of canonical JSON
nodes.community_name: Tracing an Event from Browser to Database
nodes.norm_label: event id = sha-256 of canonical json
nodes.rationale: Content-derived ID means identical event data always produces the same ID regardless of submitter, so exact re-submissions hit the D1 primary key constraint before the more expensive similarity check runs; also lets a client predict an event's ID before publishing, useful for idempotent crawler re-runs.

nodes.label: Iframe capture raced against 5s timeout
nodes.community_name: Tracing an Event from Browser to Database
nodes.rationale: Main-frame capture (allFrames:false) always finishes quickly; the iframe pass (allFrames:true) is raced against a 5-second timeout so a stuck third-party widget (Bandcamp player, Bandsintown calendar, social embed) cannot block extraction indefinitely.

nodes.label: Server-side HTML cleaning (extractCleanText)
nodes.community_name: Tracing an Event from Browser to Database
nodes.rationale: The browser captures rendered HTML (JS executed, lazy elements resolved, iframes assembled) and sends it raw; the worker cleans it server-side so cleaning logic can evolve without shipping a new extension version, and so the worker can run both JSON-LD and LLM extraction passes over the same response body.

nodes.label: Stateless crawler worker / client-side signing design
nodes.norm_label: stateless crawler worker / client-side signing design
nodes.rationale: Crawler worker returns unsigned PreparedEvents and never sees a private key; the curator's keypair lives in browser storage and all signing happens via the Web Crypto API before the event leaves the user's machine. Keeps the extraction pipeline stateless and free of identity concerns; a 401 signature failure always points to browser-side code, not the worker.

nodes.label: Obscura browser engine (opt-in, CDP)
nodes.rationale: Obscura trades some rendering fidelity on JS-heavy pages for ~85ms page loads and ~30MB memory (vs Chrome's ~500ms/~200MB), plus built-in anti-fingerprinting and tracker blocking for high-volume or bot-detection-prone crawling.

nodes.label: Geocoding via Nominatim with fallback cascade
nodes.community_name: Geocoding via Nominatim with fallback cascade
nodes.norm_label: geocoding via nominatim with fallback cascade
nodes.rationale: A cascading fallback (full address -> drop possible venue prefix -> venue+address -> venue alone -> LLM-assisted Google-search address lookup) maximizes geocode success given inconsistent address quality across scraped pages, while a module-level timestamp enforces Nominatim's 1 req/sec rate limit.

nodes.label: NormalizeFailure type & dropped_events handling
nodes.community_name: Geocoding via Nominatim with fallback cascade
nodes.rationale: Per-event normalization failures (e.g. geocoding failure) are captured in dropped_events rather than aborting the whole crawl, so partial successes are still returned to the client instead of an all-or-nothing failure.
